headlines.title: KHC Stock Forms Death Cross: Can Kraft Heinz’s New Growth Plan Power A Turnaround?
headlines.summary: Kraft Heinz reported weaker quarterly results but raised its full-year EPS outlook, increased brand investments, and set ambitious growth targets.

headlines.title: Kraft Heinz Sees Flat 2027 Sales as $700 Million Turnaround Faces a Slow Start
headlines.summary: Kraft Heinz (NASDAQ:KHC) expects organic net sales to be relatively flat in 2027 as it continues a turnaround built on higher investment in marketing, product development and innovation.

headlines.title: Coffee Unit Sale Could Be A Big Move For Kraft Heinz Stock (KHC)
headlines.summary: Kraft Heinz plans to sell its North American coffee business for US$650 million, retain a minority stake, and direct most proceeds toward debt reduction, while also reporting third quarter 2026 sales of US$6,115 million and net income of US$544 million. The planned coffee divestment simplifies Kraft Heinz’s portfolio and frees up cash for balance sheet repair at a time when the business is still absorbing goodwill and intangible asset impairments.

headlines.title: ADDING MULTIMEDIA: Kraft Heinz Outlines Path to Sustainable, Profitable Growth at 2026 Investor Day
headlines.summary: PITTSBURGH & CHICAGO, November 12, 2026--Kraft Heinz (NYSE: KHC) ("Kraft Heinz" or the "Company") is hosting its 2026 Investor Day today, where senior management will outline the Company’s strategy to deliver sustainable, volume-led profitable growth. Management will also share its financial milestones through 2029, along with initial expectations for 2027.

description: The Kraft Heinz Company, together with its subsidiaries, manufactures and markets food and beverage products in North America and internationally. Its products include condiments, sauces, dressings, and spreads; cheese, frozen potato products, and other frozen meals; meal kits, frozen snacks, and pickles; dry packaged desserts, refrigerated ready to eat desserts, and other dessert toppings; ready to drink and powdered beverages, and liquid concentrates; American sliced and recipe cheeses; mainstream coffee, coffee pods, and premium coffee; and cold cuts, bacon, and hot dogs. It offers its products under the Kraft, Oscar Mayer, Heinz, Philadelphia, Lunchables, Velveeta, Ore-Ida, Capri Sun, Maxwell House, Kool-Aid, Jell-O, ABC, Master, Quero, Golden Circle, Wattie's, Pudliszki, and Plasmon brands, as well as Bagel Bites, Claussen, A1, and Cool Whip. It sells its products through its own sales organizations, as well as through independent brokers, agents, and distributors to chain, wholesale, cooperative, and independent grocery accounts; convenience, value, and club stores; pharmacies and drug stores; mass merchants; foodservice distributors; institutions, including hotels, restaurants, bakeries, hospitals, health care facilities, and government agencies; and various e-commerce platforms and retailers. The company has a strategic partnership with the National Football League. The company was formerly known as H.J. Heinz Holding Corporation and changed its name to The Kraft Heinz Company in July 2015. The company was founded in 1869 and is headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.
